extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, picture editors, videographers and other entrants submitting work to the NPPA Best of Photojournalism 2025 competition
extracted.subtask_description: Official submission, ethical, technical and legal rules for entries to the National Press Photographers Association (NPPA) Best of Photojournalism 2025 competition, covering visual integrity, file/spec requirements, captions/metadata, eligibility, fees, and rights granted to the contest organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to NPPA Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are expected to adhere to the National Press Photographers Association Code of Ethics and its standards for visual journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code highlights (verbatim/adapted): Be accurate and comprehensive in representation of subjects; Resist being manipulated by staged photo opportunities; Be complete and provide context; Avoid stereotyping and avoid presenting one's own biases; Treat subjects with respect and dignity; Give special consideration to vulnerable subjects and compassion to victims; Intrude on private moments of grief only when public has an overriding need; While photographing do not intentionally contribute to, alter, or seek to alter or influence events; Editing should maintain the integrity of images' content and context; Do not manipulate images or add/alter sound to mislead or misrepresent; Do not pay sources or subjects or reward them materially for information/participation; Do not accept gifts/favors/compensation from those who might influence coverage; Do not intentionally sabotage efforts of other journalists; Do not engage in harassing behavior and maintain high professional behavior; Ideally: strive for access, diversity of viewpoints, avoid conflicts of interest, be unobtrusive, respect photographic moment, seek counsel when unsure, continuously study craft and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual integrity — AI and generative tools prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI generative tools to create, add, remove, expand or alter images or videos in any way is expressly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of a photograph or video clip is 'locked at the moment it is recorded.' Any generative/AI-based creation or manipulation that changes what is seen/heard is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on altering the captured scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers must not intentionally alter the scene they capture by adding, moving, removing objects or by staging or setting up situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rules: You must not add objects; You must not move/take away objects; You must not 'stage' situations (deliberately arrange objects/subjects/situations not already occurring); You must not 'set-up' situations (deliberately create situations that do not exist — e.g., bringing disparate characters together, giving or directing subjects to wear particular clothing, painting/adding objects or people); You must not ask subjects to re-enact past actions to make a photograph. These are grounds for disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed portraits/formal interviews allowed only if identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits and formal interviews may be constructed, but must be clearly identified as such and must not be presented as naturally occurring events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the photograph is a portrait the caption must make it explicitly clear that the photograph is a portrait and was posed and directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible post-processing and manipulations that disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-processing is allowed within normal limits (toning, color correction); manipulative post-processing that changes content/context is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: basic toning and color correction, correcting sensor/white balance issues. Disallowed/manipulative examples: dramatic color changes that alter original color (e.g., changing a gray sky to blue); dodging/burning or adjustments to brightness/contrast/color/saturation/sharpening/clarity that significantly alter content by obscuring, enhancing or diminishing elements; adding/moving/removing objects or people; using digital tools to alter content visible to camera. Cloning tools may be used only to remove dust spots created by lens/sensor or scanning. For audio/video: altering sequencing of audio/video to change meaning is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' right to request original files and disqualification for manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: If judges suspect manipulation, entrants may be required to submit images as recorded by the camera; failure to provide them or evidence of manipulation may lead to disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images proceeding to final stages will be requested between Feb 20 and Feb 27, 2025. Judges will discuss privately and may disqualify entries. Committee decisions about eligibility and integrity are final; awards may be vacated post-announcement if cause is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on commercially influenced/branded content and paid-for coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Filmmakers and photographers cannot be paid by anyone with a commercial stake in the story; no branded content accepted; certain team-created work may be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states: 'filmmakers and photographers cannot be paid by anyone with a commercial stake in the story, and no branded content will be accepted. Work created as a team photographer or videographer is therefore prohibited.' Entrants should avoid commercial conflicts and branded content submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry period and content eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry submission window and the timeframe during which submitted work must have been made or initially published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries accepted via portal from Dec 16, 2024 through 11:59 P.M. PT on Jan 19, 2025. All entries must have been made or initially published between Jan 1, 2024 and Dec 31, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fees and NPPA membership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee structure and membership-related rules for entry fees and waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry is free for NPPA members in good standing at contest close (Jan 19, 2025); $75 for non-members. Membership status will be checked at closing; non-members who have not paid may be disqualified. You may not use your membership to waive fees for others when entering on their behalf. On team entries, if one team member is an NPPA member, the entry fee is waived. Fee collection happens during the entry process if not a member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry limits and cross-division rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on the number of entries per entrant and restrictions on cross-division submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entrant may have up to 20 entries across any combination of disciplines and categories. Multiple entries in one category count toward the 20-entry total. A single photograph, story, video or package may not be entered on its own in more than one division, with one exception: the same video/story/package may be submitted in both Video Editing and Video Photojournalism, exclusively. No other cross-division entries are allowed. A photo may be entered in both a single category and as part of a picture story, portfolio, or compilation. A video may be entered in both a single category and as part of a compilation. Each entry counts as one toward the 20 total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Still photo technical file format and image specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Required technical specifications for still image files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images should be sized to 3000 pixels on the long dimension; saved as an RGB JPG; JPG quality setting of High (9 on a 12-point scale, 8 on a 10-point scale); file sizes should be no more than 5 MB. Do not save as CMYK. No multiple exposures, panoramas or stitched photos (in-camera or software) will be accepted. Remove any personal tags, ratings or color codes. File names in story and portfolio categories must begin with a sequence number (01, 02, etc.) so judges see them in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required IPTC metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific metadata fields that must be included with image entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following IPTC fields are required: Caption/Description (see Caption Guide); City, State/Province and Country; Date (the date the image was made); Photographer and Credit/Byline (fill both, be consistent across images); Source (your employer or client); Copyright (who holds copyright); Contact Email (use same address as account); Contact Phone (use same number as account). Including correct metadata and file formats is critical; failure may result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption content and AP-based caption rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions must be accurate, in English only, follow basic AP style, and answer the basic questions of journalism with a prescribed structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First sentence structure: describe who is in the photo and what is going on in present tense, followed by city/state/province/country as appropriate, and an absolute date (e.g., 'Monday, December 16, 2024'). Captions must give attribution of action not seen (e.g., 'according to police'). List names left-to-right; ensure clarity when multiple people are identified. The second sentence gives context or explains significance; if in doubt, omit second sentence. Try for no more than two concise sentences while including relevant information. Captions must be written in English and follow AP style. For story categories, within the caption block of the first image you must include a short overall story description (up to 100 words). If the photograph is a portrait, caption must explicitly state it is a posed/directed portrait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide original camera files on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must be prepared to provide original camera files for images that proceed to final stages when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested files will be collected between Feb 20 and Feb 27, 2025. Failure to provide these files when requested may lead to disqualification of the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture editing submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and formatting requirements for picture editing (newspaper/magazine) entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert entries to JPG files saved as RGB and not CMYK. They should be at least 3000 pixels tall. Double-page spreads should be combined into one JPG so judges can see the entire spread. Multiple-page entries should have each single page or double-page spread entered as an individual JPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital/online entries and paywall access
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit digital, online gallery, or paywalled content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital category entries should be submitted as one or more URLs. For online galleries, upload a thumbnail (when prompted) and paste links; provide login and password if the site is behind a paywall so judges can access. Presentation entries without thumbnails may be disqualified. Online entries may require a screen grab to be uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video and documentary technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required technical specs and submission steps for video/photojournalism/documentary entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All video entries should be compressed for smooth online playback. Videos must be mp4 format at 1080p resolution. Thumbnails will be required for video entries and should be 1920 x 1080 pixels in JPG format. After uploading the video, you must upload a thumbnail; video entries without thumbnails may be disqualified. Handbrake is suggested as a compression tool if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry submission process and metadata handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for uploading files, automatic caption reading from metadata, and editing during the entry flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting a category you can drag-and-drop images/videos or links. Captions will be automatically read from metadata if in the correct field; after uploading you can click NEXT to view and edit captions (e.g., remove credit info). You can change image order on the upload page. Server load may delay caption encoding/display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions granted to BOP and usage license
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants (or their employer/assignee) retain copyright but grant the Best of Photojournalism (BOP) organizers permission to reproduce, display, publish and distribute entries for contest-related and promotional/archival/educational purposes in perpetuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically grants BOP rights to execute/report/promote the contest and results, showcase via exhibitions/online displays/awards/compendiums (e.g., News Photographer Magazine), include in permanent BOP archives (NPPA/UGA servers and University of Georgia Special Collections Library), sublicense to third-parties/service providers as needed. BOP is not obligated to publish submitted entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrant warranties, representations and releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants warrant originality, right to submit, timing, and accept liability/release language related to sponsors and promotional use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrant warrants each image is original work and that they are copyright holder or authorized to submit. Entrant warrants images were taken or initially published during 2024 and submission does not breach law or third-party claims. Entrants release sponsors (e.g., Sony) from liability connected to prizes and agree BOP may share contact info with sponsors. Entrants consent to and waive claims over use of their name/likeness by BOP and sponsors for promotional/public relations related to NPPA/BOP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of rules, ethics code, and finality of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: By agreeing to terms, entrants accept contest rules and the NPPA Code of Ethics; BOP decisions are final and awards may be rescinded for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'I accept all Entry rules of the NPPA Best of Photojournalism Contest.' 'I adhere to the NPPA Code of Ethics and promise that my entries were created in accordance with its principles.' BOP is final authority on awards; entrants are not entitled to appeal. Awards may be vacated post-announcement if entries are later found in violation.
